finding: Cliniceo is cloud clinic software built specifically for aesthetic clinics, dermatologists, plastic surgeons, wellness centres and med-spas, and it lists India as a market. It is Clinozy's closest same-niche peer.
public_reaction: Capterra listing has a pros/cons section but no substantive user reviews surfaced.
our_action: Treat Cliniceo as the default comparison in sales demos; publish a 'Clinozy vs Cliniceo' page focused on floor-board, pharmacy and machine booking, which Cliniceo does not advertise.

finding: Capterra and Techjockey list a starting price of about ₹3,499–3,500 (Capterra labels it 'Flat Rate, One Time' but also says 'contact vendor'). That is a very low entry anchor for small Indian clinics.
our_action: Do not try to undercut ₹3.5k. Anchor on value instead (one recovered lead or package sale pays for a month) and offer a low-friction first tier with clear INR pricing.

finding: Cliniceo has a digital before/after photo library that it describes as giving a clear visual record of patient progress. It markets this as a core aesthetic feature.
our_action: Match it and go further: show side-by-side session comparison inside the treatment-session timeline, and add consent-gated sharing of photos over WhatsApp.

finding: The product page covers multi-session packages with per-session tracking and reminders by SMS, email or WhatsApp.
our_action: Clinozy's Offerings has packages plus a lowest-price guard. Make sure package-session consumption shows up on the Today board and at checkout so it is visibly better than Cliniceo's.

finding: Cliniceo sends invoices, prescriptions and reminders over WhatsApp, and Capterra lists WhatsApp under integrations.
our_action: Table stakes. Clinozy must ship invoice, Rx and reminder sends on WhatsApp on day one, and also offer two-way chat in Leads, which Cliniceo appears to use only for outbound sends.

finding: Cliniceo's site has patient counselling screens and quotations: a counsellor builds a priced treatment plan and the patient receives it. Clinozy has a Counsellor role and Leads, but the brief lists no quotation or estimate object.
public_reaction: Testimonial on the vendor site calls it 'one of the best CRMs for skin and aesthetic clinics'.
our_action: Build a 'Treatment plan / Quotation' in Leads and Patients that converts into a package with one click, and track quote-to-conversion rate in Reporting.

finding: Aesthetic peers (Cliniceo per Capterra, Consentz and others) market digital consent forms with before/after documentation. Clinozy's brief does not mention consent forms.
our_action: Add procedure-specific e-consent with signature capture, attached to the treatment session and photos, and sendable over WhatsApp before the visit.

finding: Capterra lists Cliniceo as English-only.
our_action: Lead with Clinozy's Hindi and 10 other languages for front-desk staff and therapists. That is a real edge in Tier-2 and Tier-3 Indian cities.

finding: Cliniceo claims '100+ top aesthetic clinics across India', but almost no independent reviews exist on Capterra, G2 or app stores. Buyers have little social proof to go on.
public_reaction: Very few public reviews found. That thin footprint is itself a signal.
our_action: Seed early social proof aggressively: get video testimonials from launch clinics, Google reviews and Capterra reviews within the first 90 days, and fill the review vacuum before Cliniceo does.

finding: Cliniceo's public material shows no in-house pharmacy with batch and expiry tracking, MR management or purchase orders. Indian derma clinics that dispense would need a second tool.
our_action: Message 'one system from enquiry to pharmacy counter'. Demo dispensing at checkout with batch and expiry, because Cliniceo cannot show it.

finding: Before/after libraries work through visible progress (the goal-gradient effect) and social proof. Patients who see their own improvement stay in multi-session courses, and clinics use the images as proof to sell to new leads.
psychology: Goal-gradient and progress visibility, plus social proof for prospects.
our_action: Beat it by automatically sending a 'your progress' photo pair on WhatsApp after session N of M ('3 of 6 done'), with consent. That turns photos into a retention habit loop rather than a passive archive.

finding: A ₹3.5k flat or one-time-looking price uses a low anchor and reduces fear of commitment in owner-run clinics that dislike recurring SaaS fees.
psychology: Price anchoring and aversion to subscriptions or losses.
our_action: Counter with a no-lock-in monthly plan, a free data import, and an ROI calculator ('missed leads × average package value'), so the comparison is about money recovered rather than sticker price.

finding: Clinicea has strong ratings (4.9/5 from 31 reviews on Capterra and Software Advice), and reviewers repeatedly praise the support staff's professionalism.
public_reaction: Reviewer: support staff are professional; several reviewers say they have 'no complaints'.
our_action: Support is the moat in this tier. Offer WhatsApp-based human support with SLA, named onboarding managers for the first 50 clinics, and publish response times.

finding: Dermatology users praise Clinicea's 'easy billing, package management and session consumption'. Packages can be predefined or built on the fly, and the system prevents rebooking a completed session.
public_reaction: Derm clinic reviewer: 'easy billing, package management and session consumption'.
our_action: Copy the 'no rebooking a consumed session' guard and on-the-fly package creation at checkout, then surface remaining sessions on the patient card and the Today board.

finding: Clinicea links SMS reminders to both appointments and recalls, so lapsed patients get pulled back automatically.
our_action: Clinozy's Recall views plus automation rules ('Let Clinozy handle') should send WhatsApp-first recall nudges per treatment (for example, a peel every 4 weeks) out of the box.

finding: Clinicea is used across 20 specialities on five continents, with dermatology and aesthetic as core niches. It brings mature, multi-country credibility.
our_action: Do not fight on breadth. Position Clinozy as built only for skin, hair and aesthetic clinics in India, which is deeper than a 20-speciality tool.

finding: Users ask for two-way WhatsApp. One reviewer's only complaint was that 'it would be better if they support 2-way Whatsapp Communication'.
public_reaction: 'It would be better if they support 2-way Whatsapp Communication.'
our_action: Make two-way WhatsApp inside Leads and Patients a headline differentiator, with Mine/Unreplied views and SLA timers on unreplied chats.

finding: Reviewers say an Android app would be beneficial, which suggests no native Android app for staff.
public_reaction: Reviewer suggestion: an Android app would be beneficial.
our_action: Make sure Clinozy's PWA is installable and fast on low-end Android phones (offline-tolerant Today board, push notifications), and market it as 'works on the receptionist's phone'.

finding: Reviewers complain they cannot open a patient profile directly from the calendar, and one found case sheets hard to use because they lack nested forms.
public_reaction: Complaints: cannot open the patient profile from the calendar; case sheet lacks nested forms.
our_action: Make every appointment chip on the calendar and Today board one click to the patient, and keep EMR templates derma-specific and nested (lesion → site → grade).

finding: One reviewer reports that bill deletion did not work completely. Billing edge cases erode trust with accountants.
public_reaction: Reviewer: bill deletion not working completely.
our_action: Use void-and-credit-note flows (never hard deletes) with an audit log. Market Clinozy's audit log and GST-correct credit notes to owners and accountants.

finding: Clinicea's pricing is per user (about $59–69/user/month listed) and quote-only after a demo. That is expensive and opaque for Indian clinics with many front-desk staff and therapists.
our_action: Publish transparent INR pricing per branch rather than per seat, so adding therapists, counsellors or a pharmacist costs nothing. Per-seat pricing hits Clinozy's role-rich model hardest.

finding: Users report limited pathology and lab features in Clinicea, which shows that derma clinics do order labs (for example, hormonal panels for acne or hair loss). Clinozy's brief has no lab or investigation module.
our_action: Add simple lab orders and result attachments to the patient record. Build a full LIS later, if ever.

finding: Prepaid packages with visible session consumption create commitment and sunk cost: patients who prepaid for six sessions come back. Clinics get cash up front, and that 'locks in' revenue.
psychology: Commitment and consistency, sunk-cost effect, and endowment from prepaid credit.
our_action: Go beyond tracking. Show patients their remaining sessions and an expiry countdown on WhatsApp ('2 sessions left, valid till 30 Nov'). Loss aversion then drives rebooking, which Clinicea does not market.

finding: High ratings driven by human support show that small clinics fear complexity and value reassurance. A responsive person reduces the anxiety of switching more than any feature does.
public_reaction: Reviewers praise support professionalism above features.
psychology: Risk and uncertainty reduction; trust through human reciprocity.
our_action: Offer 'we migrate your Excel or old software data for you' and a 30-day hand-holding period, and use the View-as role preview in demos to show that each role sees a simple screen.

finding: DoctorsApp dominates Indian search for 'dermatology clinic software India', with dozens of SEO pages and blogs ('best', 'top 10', 'affordable', 'ABDM compliant') that mostly rank itself first.
public_reaction: Little independent reaction. The ratings shown are self-published on its own pages.
our_action: Invest early in Indian SEO and GEO content for skin, hair and aesthetic long-tail terms (laser booking, derma pharmacy, hair transplant CRM), plus honest comparison pages. DoctorsApp shows that this channel works and is under-contested by quality content.

finding: DoctorsApp publishes simple annual plans: Silver at ₹8,999/yr and Gold at ₹14,999/yr, inclusive of taxes and with 'no hidden fees'. Techjockey lists ₹10,999/yr.
our_action: Publish clear annual INR pricing with GST included and a discount for annual payment. Indian doctors compare on yearly sticker price.

finding: DoctorsApp markets an AI voice prescription and AI medical scribe for dermatologists ('generate dermatology Rx within 30 seconds').
our_action: Clinozy's brief has no AI. Add voice-to-prescription in Hindi and English with derma templates, because doctor time is the scarcest resource in a busy skin OPD.

finding: DoctorsApp claims AI-assisted imaging that 'captures, analyses and tracks skin conditions' and suggests diagnoses from uploaded images.
our_action: Do not over-claim diagnosis because of regulatory and liability risk. Do add AI photo tagging and alignment for before/after comparison.

finding: DoctorsApp pushes ABDM compliance (India's national digital health stack) for dermatology EMR. Clinozy's brief does not mention ABDM or ABHA.
our_action: Plan ABDM/ABHA linking (HIP registration) as a trust and compliance badge for Indian clinics, especially for selling to hospital-attached derma departments.

finding: DoctorsApp offers a mobile app for doctors with speech-to-prescription, so doctors can consult from a phone.
our_action: Make Clinozy's doctor view mobile-first: today's patients, Rx and photos on the doctor's phone.

finding: DoctorsApp is an EMR/OPD and HMIS tool for doctors. Its pages emphasise records, Rx and IPD, not lead CRM, WhatsApp conversations, counselling or package conversion, which drive aesthetic-clinic revenue.
our_action: Message 'DoctorsApp is for documenting patients; Clinozy is for growing the clinic', and show the lead → consult → package → recall funnel.

finding: Its content is heavily self-promotional (it ranks itself #1 on its own 'top 10' lists), and its self-published ratings vary across pages, which can erode trust with careful buyers.
public_reaction: No Reddit or independent practitioner reviews found for DoctorsApp.
our_action: Win on authenticity: real clinic case studies with names and metrics, and third-party reviews. Avoid fake 'top 10' content.

finding: DoctorsApp is generalist software (multi-speciality, with derma as one vertical). There is no evidence of machine/laser-room scheduling or consumable usage per procedure.
our_action: Demo booking by doctor, room and laser machine plus consumable usage per procedure. Generalist EMRs cannot show these aesthetic-specific operations.

finding: Techjockey reports DoctorsApp is used by more than 1,400 doctors and 70+ hospitals across India and six countries, giving it a modest installed base and references.
our_action: Expect DoctorsApp in competitive deals with solo dermatologists. Target multi-chair aesthetic clinics and chains, where its OPD focus is weakest.

finding: 'AI Rx in 30 seconds' appeals to doctors' identity and status (a modern, tech-forward practice) and to time scarcity, while also signalling that the product is future-proof.
psychology: Status and identity signalling; time-scarcity relief; novelty bias.
our_action: Beat it with demonstrable outcomes rather than buzzwords: a live demo of a 20-second Hindi voice Rx that auto-adds the medicines to the pharmacy dispense queue, so the AI ties into revenue.

finding: 'Cheapest' and 'affordable' framing with tax-inclusive annual pricing targets small clinics' price sensitivity and fear of hidden costs.
psychology: Fear of hidden costs; price anchoring; simplicity heuristic.
our_action: Use the same transparent, GST-inclusive framing, and add a 'what you'd pay for 3 tools' comparison (EMR + WhatsApp CRM + pharmacy) to reframe Clinozy as cheaper in total.

finding: Picky Assist sells a WhatsApp-first solution for derma clinics: a chatbot that qualifies leads by collecting the concern, desired procedure, budget and photos, then books consultations and sends reminders, consent forms and invoices.
our_action: Copy the qualifying flow. Add a WhatsApp intake bot in Leads that collects concern, area, budget and photos before a human counsellor replies, and shows them on the lead card.

finding: It has a dedicated hair-transplant offering that handles 'the complete hair transplant experience end-to-end on WhatsApp' (enquiry, scalp photos, graft estimate, booking, post-op care).
our_action: Build a hair-transplant journey template: scalp photo intake, graft-count quote, surgery-day checklist and post-op day-1/7/30 WhatsApp care messages.

finding: Picky Assist has a free plan (with a 30% markup on WhatsApp messages) and low entry pricing (from about ₹999/month for API-only, ₹2,499–3,999 for Pro and Ultimate, per its 2026 blog). Sources conflict with its USD pricing page.
our_action: Bundle WhatsApp API setup into Clinozy at no extra platform fee and pass Meta charges through at cost. Clinics hate double-paying for a CRM and a separate WhatsApp vendor.

finding: Its derma page claims '50% fewer no-shows with WhatsApp reminders' and '75% higher conversion from interest to consultation'. Clinozy has no published outcome metrics.
our_action: Instrument Clinozy so every clinic sees its own no-show rate and lead-to-consult conversion before and after go-live, then publish anonymised benchmarks.

finding: Picky Assist offers chatbot automation (no-code flows, auto-replies) that answers FAQs at night. Clinozy's automation rules are task-based, not conversational.
our_action: Add an after-hours WhatsApp auto-responder plus FAQ bot (prices, timings, location, procedure info) that hands over to a counsellor in the morning with context.

finding: Picky Assist is a messaging layer, not clinic software. It has no EMR, pharmacy, stock, GST ledger or room/machine booking, so clinics must stitch it to other systems.
our_action: Message 'WhatsApp that already knows the patient': every chat in Clinozy shows packages, balance, last photos and next appointment, which a standalone bot cannot do.

finding: There are essentially no independent reviews. G2 says 'not enough reviews', and Capterra and Software Advice show zero ratings.
public_reaction: No user reviews found. That is a signal of low visibility and trust.
our_action: Earn the public reviews Picky Assist lacks, and highlight them on comparison pages.

finding: Pricing is confusing: a USD pricing page dated Nov 2025 ($29–69/month) conflicts with an INR 2026 blog (₹999–3,999), and the free plan carries a 30% message markup.
our_action: Show one INR price with an example monthly bill (platform plus estimated WhatsApp charges), so the cost is predictable.

finding: Instant WhatsApp replies exploit speed-to-lead: aesthetic enquiries are impulsive and comparison-shopped, so the first clinic to respond wins (a recency and reciprocity effect).
psychology: Speed-to-lead; reciprocity; reducing the impulsive buyer's window to shop around.
our_action: Show an 'Unreplied for N minutes' timer and escalation in the Leads view, and auto-acknowledge within seconds. Then make the human follow-up visibly accountable per counsellor in Reporting.

finding: Asking for budget and photos early creates micro-commitments (foot-in-the-door): a patient who has shared photos is more invested and more likely to book.
our_action: Replicate it in Clinozy's intake bot, then reply with a counsellor message that references their photos, making the patient feel personally assessed.

finding: Automated reminders reduce no-shows through implementation intentions (a concrete time, place and confirm button) and through the social cost of declining a personal-feeling message.
psychology: Implementation intentions; commitment through an explicit 'Confirm' reply.
our_action: Use WhatsApp interactive buttons (Confirm / Reschedule) that update Clinozy's Appointments and Today board live, closing a loop Picky Assist cannot close without integration.

finding: TeleCRM is an Indian lead and tele-calling CRM that explicitly targets hair-transplant clinics, keeping inquiries, follow-ups and appointment tracking in one place.
public_reaction: G2 (10 reviews, 4.6): praise for having WhatsApp messaging and lead tracking in one place.
our_action: Clinozy's Leads must support high-volume calling teams: call logging, follow-up dates, lead stage and source (Meta ads, Google, Practo), plus duplicate merging.

finding: TeleCRM includes a built-in auto-dialer and call recordings in its per-user plans, which matters to hair-transplant clinics running call-centre style sales.
our_action: Gap for Clinozy: add click-to-call with Indian cloud telephony (Exotel, Knowlarity, MCUBE) and call-recording links on the lead timeline.

finding: TeleCRM sells call-centre telephony (auto-dialer, recordings, call analytics) as core. Clinozy's brief lists WhatsApp conversations but no calling or telephony.
our_action: Prioritise a telephony integration plus 'call outcome' tasks. Indian hair and aesthetic leads are still converted by phone.

finding: TeleCRM costs about ₹749–1,049 per user/month (annual or quarterly), with a 3-user minimum and a ₹1,999 one-time WhatsApp API setup fee.
our_action: Benchmark: a 5-counsellor hair clinic pays about ₹4–5k/month for TeleCRM alone. Price Clinozy's full suite so it beats 'TeleCRM + EMR + billing' combined.

finding: Reliability complaints: a Feb 2025 Capterra India review (1/5) cites app glitches, missed customer messages, a WhatsApp bot that stopped working, and weak after-sales support.
public_reaction: 'Poor' CRM: glitches, missed messages, WhatsApp bot stopped working, weak support (Capterra India, Feb 2025).
our_action: Make WhatsApp delivery health visible (sent/delivered/failed, template status) and alert on failures. Reliability is the claim to own.

finding: A Techjockey reviewer complained that data cannot be accessed or updated without an internet connection.
public_reaction: Reviewer: cannot access or update info without internet.
our_action: Give the Clinozy PWA offline tolerance for the Today board and check-in (queue changes and sync later). Patchy clinic Wi-Fi is common in India.

finding: TeleCRM is a horizontal sales CRM with no clinical records, before/after photos, graft or session tracking, pharmacy or GST billing. Clinics must run a second system after conversion.
our_action: Message 'no handoff gap': a lead converts to a patient in one click with the full chat history, quote and photos carried over.

finding: Per-user pricing with a 3-user minimum punishes clinics that want every receptionist and therapist on the system.
our_action: Price per branch or clinic with unlimited staff. That is a strong message for role-rich clinics.

finding: Auto-dialers and follow-up queues build a habit loop for counsellors (next lead → call → log → next) and create accountability through manager dashboards, so 'nobody forgets to call back'.
public_reaction: G2 reviewers value 'lead tracking in one place'.
psychology: Habit loop; accountability and social monitoring; reduced decision fatigue for staff.
our_action: Clinozy's desk work queue and Tasks should give one 'Next best action' button per counsellor, with streaks and leaderboards on conversions (tied to commissions) to make the loop sticky.

finding: Owners of high-ticket hair-transplant clinics (₹50k–2L procedures) fear losing leads they paid for through Meta ads. CRMs sell to that loss aversion with 'never miss a lead' messaging.
psychology: Loss aversion over ad spend; control and visibility needs of owners.
our_action: Build an owner dashboard showing 'ad leads not contacted in 24h' and an estimate of revenue at risk, framing Clinozy as protecting their ad spend.

finding: Zavis (UAE, founded 2025) is an AI front desk for dermatology and aesthetic clinics. It captures leads from WhatsApp, Instagram and web, qualifies them with AI, and books directly into the clinic's EMR.
our_action: Signal of where the peer tier is heading. Plan an AI lead-qualifier and booking agent on top of Clinozy's own calendar, which is native rather than bolted on.

finding: Zavis offers Arabic and English voice AI receptionists and missed-call recovery (an auto WhatsApp follow-up when a call is missed).
our_action: Build missed-call → WhatsApp auto-message ('Sorry we missed you, book here') via telephony webhooks. It is cheap and high-impact for Indian clinics, and Hindi or regional voice AI can come later.

finding: Zavis sends WhatsApp payment links so patients pay deposits for bookings inside the chat. Clinozy's brief has Stripe for its own SaaS billing but no patient-side UPI or payment links.
our_action: Add UPI/Razorpay payment links in WhatsApp for booking deposits and package payments, and post them automatically to the Payments ledger.

finding: Zavis has a unified inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram and web. Clinozy's Leads covers WhatsApp conversations, and Instagram DMs are a major enquiry source for aesthetic clinics.
our_action: Add Instagram DM and Meta lead-form ingestion into Leads, with source attribution.

finding: Zavis integrates with existing clinic systems such as Clinicea, sitting on top of the EMR rather than replacing it.
our_action: Clinozy's outbound webhooks plus a public API could let AI front-desk tools plug in. Alternatively, own the layer natively and position against 'yet another add-on'.

finding: Zavis is quote-only: pricing comes after a 20-minute walkthrough and depends on locations, volume and modules. That is opaque and likely premium.
our_action: Publish transparent self-serve pricing, which suits small Indian clinics that will not sit through sales calls.

finding: Zavis is UAE-focused (Arabic, Dubai licensing, UAE team). There is no evidence of an India launch, Hindi support, GST or INR pricing.
our_action: Own 'AI front desk for Indian skin clinics' before Zavis or similar Gulf players expand. Hindi and Hinglish chat and GST invoices are the moat.

finding: Zavis is a front-desk and communication layer only, with no pharmacy, stock, EMR or ledger, so it depends on a separate clinic system.
our_action: Message 'AI that can see your stock, packages and payments'. For example, the bot can tell a patient their package balance or that a product is in stock.

finding: A 24/7 AI receptionist sells to fear of missing out on lost bookings ('every missed call is a lost patient') and to relief from staff dependence and attrition.
psychology: Loss aversion and FOMO on missed revenue; desire for control and less reliance on staff.
our_action: Counter-message with a balanced 'AI plus your team' story. AI handles after-hours and first touch, and Clinozy shows the hand-off and outcomes, which reassures owners who distrust bots talking to high-ticket patients.

finding: Zavis leans on named logos (Modern Aesthetics, Lueur Aesthetic Clinic, Dental Nation) and '150+ clinics' social proof to de-risk a new 2025 product.
psychology: Social proof and authority by association.
our_action: Clinozy should launch with a founding-clinic programme (discount for logo and case-study rights), so it has named Indian derma logos at launch.
